slides.0.title: Winemaking and terroir in depth
slides.0.subtitle: Malbec styles by altitude and soil, Torrontés, sparkling wine and blends
slides.1.title: How altitude changes Malbec
slides.1.highlights.0.title: High altitude
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Thicker skins (colour and tannin), retained acid and intense aromatics; Malbec shows violet, black and blue fruit, plush tannin and floral lift (WSET study material)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Low, hot sites
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Very ripe fruit with softer acid, and a risk of jammy Malbec
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Differing lapse rates
slides.1.highlights.2.content: About 0.6°C per 100 m (Wine With Seth) or about 0.8°C (The Drinks Business quoting Chandon), so it is not tested
slides.1.content: Altitude is like a timer: the same variety is generous low down and tight and fresh higher up.
slides.2.title: Comparing regional styles
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Luján de Cuyo and Maipú
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Luján de Cuyo: mid-high altitude, classic, structured and age-worthy; Maipú: lower and warmer, ripe, with a broad quality range
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The Uco Valley
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The highest major Mendoza zone: Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Chardonnay with elegance and acidity; Gualtallary is "more austerity than exuberance", Altamira elegant and tense, Vista Flores lush and ripe (Decanter 2019)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Cafayate and Patagonia
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Cafayate: high-altitude Torrontés and some intense reds; Patagonia: cool and windy, with Pinot Noir, fresher Malbec and Merlot, and aromatic whites
slides.2.content: When comparing styles, altitude, soil and warmth are the three main threads.
slides.3.title: Torrontés, sparkling and blends
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Torrontés
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Intense rose, geranium and peach; it can taste bitter if overcropped or grown hot; Cafayate's cool nights at altitude preserve acid and perfume
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Sparkling wine
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Chandon was founded in 1959 (LVMH), starting with vineyards at 1,000 m, and holds about 90% of the Argentine sparkling market; vineyards at 1,200 m and above use the traditional method with 18 months to 5 years on lees; it also uses Charmat (The Drinks Business, 2019)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: High-altitude sparkling
slides.3.highlights.2.content: At 1,200 m and above no tartaric acid is needed; above 1,600 m total acidity is 13–14 g/L, pH is below 3 and nearly all wines go through malolactic fermentation
slides.3.content: Argentina's sparkling wine and Torrontés both rely on altitude to keep acidity.
What is the main effect of high altitude on Malbec?
A. Thicker skins, retained acid and intense aromatics
Skins thicken and acid is retained.
Which area is often described as giving classic, structured, age-worthy Malbec?
A. When overcropped or grown too hot
Overcropping or heat makes it bitter.
